correctness.rationale: The addition theorem identifies evaluation ranks with the 12-by-12 Legendre Gram ranks, whose exact integer inner products are reconstructed. Rational Legendre recurrence and exact elimination prove ranks 1,3,5,7,9,11,9 through degree six; strict exact Sylvester certificates prove all other degrees seven to one hundred positive definite with a uniform 1/10000 lower eigenvalue bound except seventeen. At seventeen, an exact constant eigenvalue 462143232/4177248169415651 is positive below 1e-6 and a separate exact complement inequality proves it uniquely minimal. The validated Bernstein bound plus rational row-sum upper bounds and Gershgorin proves the infinite tail from 101. Trace twelve yields the unique worst condition number. No finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: A complete rank-and-stability theorem for twelve canonical Archimedean sampling nodes is a natural intrinsic invariant. It proves a nonmonotone low-degree rank regression, permanent recovery of exact-degree interpolation, and a uniquely extreme later stability collapse with exact eigenvalue and global separation. These are object-motivated structural facts, not arbitrary finite tabulation or an unsupported tiny improvement.
